headline: Reddit tests audio and video experience similar to TikTok
summary: Users can soon listen to Reddit posts in the background or watch them come to life with video, mirroring popular content formats on other platforms.
details: Reddit is beginning to test a new "video Reddit" experience, allowing users to listen to posts in the background or watch them with accompanying video. This feature aims to bring viral stories to life in formats similar to those found on platforms like TikTok and Meta's Reels.

The company announced plans for narrated Reddit videos during its second-quarter earnings call, with CEO Steve Huffman noting the growing trend of consuming Reddit content on other social media. The goal is to make spoken Reddit content more engaging for users.

Initial tests will focus on select English-language communities and will be accessible via Reddit's iOS and Android apps. Users will have the option to choose between "read" or "play" modes when available.

These new formats will not replace the original text-based posts or comment sections. Instead, they offer an alternative way to consume content, whether users are exercising, commuting, or simply prefer an audio-visual experience.

Reddit has previously experimented with video features, including native video hosting and a TikTok-style feed. Video in comments has also seen success, now accounting for over 10% of video posts on the platform.

topic: amazon trashing rare books to train AI
headline_marked: [[Amazon destroying rare books]] to train AI, Airtag reveals
headline: Amazon destroying rare books to train AI, Airtag reveals
summary: An Airtag hidden in a rare book tracked to an Amazon AI facility in Las Vegas, where books are reportedly torn apart for training data.
details: An investigation using a hidden Airtag has revealed that Amazon is purchasing rare books in bulk and destroying them to train its AI models. The Airtag, planted in a rare book by a bookseller, was tracked to an Amazon AI training facility in Las Vegas.

Sources indicate that the team at the facility, known as VGT3, is focused on tearing books from their spines and scanning pages. A logo on the warehouse door depicted a Tyrannosaurus rex preparing to devour a book, a detail that has drawn criticism.

Amazon has stated that it "purchases books through commercial channels to help develop and improve the products and services our customers use," but declined to comment specifically on AI training. This practice is controversial, with critics like Michael Burry reportedly calling it "evil incarnate."

The need for unique training data is high as Amazon competes with firms like Google and OpenAI. Reports suggest that Amazon's AI team may have faced a shortage of books for scanning, raising concerns about the systematic destruction of valuable historical and intellectual works.

Booksellers suspect AI firms are targeting books with ISBN numbers to ensure a high volume of unique works in training datasets. Workers at the Amazon facility were reportedly trained to scan barcodes or ISBNs before scanning books, lending credence to this theory.
